newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes range bound late, moderate demand seen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes range bound late, moderate demand seen.

text.p: U.S. domestic grades traded narrowly amid moderate refiner demand late Friday, supported by a shut Atlantic arbitrage, traders said.
A refiner surfaced for decent volumes on Light Louisiana Sweet/St James, taking 5,000 to 6,000 barrel-per-day parcels at West Texas Intermediate plus 40 to 41 cents.
The grade fared slightly better than Thursday, inching up a couple cents due to scant North Sea alternatives.
The same interest was sighted for Midland sweet grades with two refiners taking small lots at WTI plus 7/8 cents.
November WTI/Cushing was assessed at $24.55-65 a barrel.
Overall, cash crude business remained subdued with some Oct/Nov spread trade seen in West Texas Sour/Midland and a handful of business in WTI/Cushing Posting Plus.
Postings Plus traded at $2.35/2.36 a barrel, barely changed from Thursday, but with levels improving over the day along with the firmer Oct/Nov WTI spread.
The Oct/Nov spread rose to 65 cents, up about 10 cents.
Refiners are expected to maintain relatively high runs to meet with heating oil demand and low stocks, which look set to underpin domestic grade differentials, traders said.
Sours, however, could be more prone to pressure from a rise in Latin American cargoes to the U.S. Gulf and a more workable import arbitrage.
